utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Good morning, Madam Registrar. Could you kindly call the case, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is case number IT-05-88-T, the Prosecutor versus Vujadin Popovic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam. All the accused are here. If there are problems with interpretation, please let me know straight away. The situation as regards Defence teams is exactly the same as it was yesterday, same with Prosecution. I take there are no preliminaries. Lieutenant Colonel, good morning to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning, sir.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Welcome back. We will do our utmost to finish with your testimony today. Mr. Ostojic will conclude his cross-examination within 15 minutes as he indicated yesterday or there about, probably shorter time, in a shorter time, and then we will see about the rest. Go ahead, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good morning, Lieutenant Colonel Egbers. Sir, I'd like to cover a couple points that we may have touched upon yesterday for further clarification. First of all, if I can ask you, do you recall forming an impression or being told that the Bosnian Serbs were questioning Bosnian Muslims during the period from the 12th through the 17th of 1995, and when I say "questioning" I mean interrogating.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me whether I was told or I've seen?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Or you formed your own impression?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I saw was -- it was a table on the football field. That's the only thing that could have pointed to a kind of interrogation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Can we switch -- quickly go to your debriefing with the Royal Netherlands Army, and as we discussed yesterday that was 2D00022. I'll direct your attention again to the 6th page of that document, specifically paragraph number 5. And let me know, sir, when you've received it on the ELMO or the e-court system?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Is that the handwritten report?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I believe it's typewritten in Dutch by you and then it's translated -- typed out -- I don't believe that that's the correct one. But if I could read it into the record I think the witness will understand given the time constraints. Sir, yesterday we spoke about - trying just to refresh your recollection, I apologise for bringing it up again - the word "fanatical BiH fighters." It was in that paragraph or that text, two paragraphs above that that was in one paragraph above that, I'm sorry, paragraph 6, you state, "Major Zoran told me that there was a large group of BiH fighters in the area of KV," and then there is a series of numbers.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Following that you write, "It appears from the questioning of prisoners of war by the BSA that two groups of BiH fighters exist," and then there is more text. I'm just focussing on that sentence. When you state there, sir, that it appears from the questioning of prisoners of war, did you formulate that impression or was that told to you by Mr. Major Zoran Malinic?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I told you yesterday, paragraph 6, 7, and 8 were all told by me by this Major Zoran and he was the one who said, "No, you can't leave because there is something going on in the hills," and that's the story he told me. And the story he told me was written down by me when I entered the enclave again after being there for two days. So this was his way of telling us, Stay here, we can't let you go.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you independently verify whether or not the Bosnian Serbs were interrogating or questioning captured Bosnian Muslims?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen any interrogation of the Bosnian Muslims. The thing he said to me was that he had the information and that's why we had to stay there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was that the extent of your discussion with him on this topic or was there anything else that comes to mind as you sit here today?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no discussion with him at that day. He was just explaining to me why he thought it wasn't safe for us to return back to Bratunac and to the enclave and when I see -- when I written down KV -- the numbers, those are square kilometres on a map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Usher, 2D23 page 3.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I don't think he's referring to what's on right now. It was a tight --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think we have it clear enough for the record unless the court would like it on the e-court screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think it would be better if we had it. Anyway, let's proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Switching topics quickly I'd like to focus on the 2000 interview that you had with the OTP investigators. That would be 30th of April of 2000. Okay? That was immediately after your Krstic trial as we established yesterday. Can you share with us how it is that you came back to visit with two investigators here at the ICTY? Did they initiate the call or did you call them?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they initiated the call.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I was called to come here and to -- because they were investigating this Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And who called you, sir, and what did they tell you during this phone conversation?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that, they just asked me to come.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And it was a Sunday afternoon, I think you said, correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How long was the meeting? I couldn't get that from the transcript yesterday. I don't know that you answered and I apologise in advance if you did.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know it couldn't be longer than an hour that I've been here, including the coffee.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, at that time, sir, did they give you your statement that you'd previously given to the ICTY and the Office of the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that but I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, were you shown at that April 30th, 2000, meeting with the Office of the Prosecutor and her investigators whether -- were you shown a photo album with various pictures in it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not what I can recall, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Were you shown any individual still or picture of someone who purports to be Mr. Beara?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only recall that I have seen the video that they have shown you yesterday.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So it was limited to that one video, correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I can recall, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And how many times did you have to watch that video before you were convinced, as you say, that it was Mr. Beara in that video?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I've seen it several times but you would like to emphasise that I only recognised him the last time I saw the video but as you see it's a very small -- short tape and it was a Sunday so I have tried to watch it very accurate. That's why I saw it several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Well how many is several to you, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I thought it was in the statement as well and I think you're referring to that, that it was seven or eight times.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And after how many times did you confirm that it was Mr. Beara?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was no -- yesterday I've seen it twice and because after -- it's a very short tape so I say, Well, let's see it again. Who else is on the tape, so I didn't only seen the tape just to recognise Colonel Beara.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How long was that tape, do you remember?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Few minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think the tape is 54 minutes in length, the entire tape. Did the ICTY investigators ask you to look at this random tape and invite you, sir, with the control to stop when, if at all, you might see Mr. Beara? Is that the way it worked? Or in fact did they set it, sir, on the time in which they suggested to you that that person in that parade or ceremony may have been Mr. Beara? Which way did it work?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there was a short video shown to me, like it was yesterday. There was the exact video. It wasn't seven or eight times the 45 minutes. That's all I can declare about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, let me switch topics quickly and back to Major Zoran Malinic, if I may. When you were there for approximately two days during your stay with Major Zoran Malinic, did he inform you, sir, that he could not control the other military groups outside the school confines in Nova Kasaba?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he told me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And did you independently verify that at all?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was no way for me to verify the things he told me. He said, "Well, we have to wait for my Colonel Beara because he's the one who can guarantee your safety when you're going back to the enclave of Srebrenica."

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, was Major Zoran able to guarantee your safety?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And can you share with us, sir, how were you treated during those two days in Nova Kasaba, the school that you mentioned on the 13th and 14th of July 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was treated well. We were, of course, restricted in the things we could do, the Major asked us, Well, okay, you can leave if you want to so we left with three vehicles but we came back with only one, as I declared two days ago. So the treatment was okay and I didn't have the -- I didn't have the idea of being kept there with a gun on my head but there were soldiers who were aiming their guns at us and we were not free of course to go back and the story what he told me was that it was for my own safety to be there but I had no possibility to go back as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, wouldn't the independent verification be that you were not restricted, you were able to leave, you sent three vehicles outside of the school compound or outside of the school premises and you found out that in fact it was confirmed what Major Zoran Malinic told you, he had no control and it was not safe for you to leave that area? Isn't that accurate?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know whether he had control about troops in the nearance [phoen] of the school but the only thing I can tell you is that we tried to go back, we were stopped by soldiers who had AK 47s pointed at us, they still in their vehicles and we got back.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: What was your impression of Major Zoran? Was he an honest individual or did he mislead you when he said that he had no control of the troops outside of the premises of the school?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, he told me a story about Muslims killing each other in the school in the nearance of the school being a threat to us. I don't think that there was the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth, when I look back at that time from this position. So if you ask me if he was an honest man, do you want me to have a look at him the way I see him now? Because I don't think that was completely honest.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please make longer pauses between question and answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Currently or at that time? That would be sufficient. If --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We got a message.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I got it.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was that a correct answer?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's not for me to decide. Okay, thank you, though, for checking with me. Sir, who -- strike that. Isn't it true that on the second day you requested that you and your men be returned to Potocari and you requested it to Major Zoran Malinic, correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've made the first -- the first day, I complained about our cars being stolen, our cars taken away from us. I've always during those two days complained about it and I've always tried to manage to get back to the compound, back to the headquarters of the UN. So it's the first and the second day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So it was at your request, correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was at my request that we went back.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. And also it was at your request that you unfortunately had to leave the two Mercedes vehicles behind, correct? It was your decision?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The two lost Mercedes were my decision yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It was also your decision to have the Bosnian Serbs who were at that school escort you in their vehicle, correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct because this Major Zoran, he arranged my returning.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't ask him to bring me with his BOVs.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Didn't you prefer it, though?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd rather go back with my own vehicles and my own soldiers towards the compound. That was what I preferred.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you did not prefer it, right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no opportunity for me to decide whether to go back with my own -- with own cars, with my own troops to the compound. It was -- because of the all the cars that we used were stolen at that time so it was my -- it was my -- I went with this BOV towards the compound but it wasn't the ideal situation, of course, leaving two cars behind.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I direct your attention to your first statement, the 24th of October 1995, to the ICTY, page 7 for the Court and my learned colleague, towards the lower portion, and I'll read the paragraph and I hope we will come on the ELMO. It's 2D00019 or on the e-court. "In the evening I requested to be taken back to Potocari in one of the Bosnian Serbs' armoured vehicles." We talked about that, right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll read it with you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Page 7. Thank you. Towards the lower portion, second to the bottom paragraph. This is your statement, sir, from the 24th of October 1995, several months after the events that we are discussing here today, "In the evening I requested to be taken back to Potocari in one of the Bosnian Serbian armoured vehicle. I preferred to be driven by them than to drive one of our own vehicles because our safety would thus be ensured." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is that also inaccurate, sir?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps your memory is what's somewhat skewed?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you asked me -- you just asked me whether it was my decision to take the BOV but it was -- were, of course, the circumstances that made me no other possibility to get into the BOVs. So when it was safe for us to drive, when nobody should steal the vehicles the UN used, when there were no Bosnian Serbs in blue, with blue helmets in white APCs on the road, it would have been safe for us to go back but we didn't have any choice. I made a decision to leave two Mercedes behind and the only thing we could do is get a ride back to the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think I understand. Thank you, Lieutenant Colonel. Now, sir, going back to formulating your impression that Mr. Beara was the commander of Major Zoran Malinic, that was really your impression, isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what he told me. He said there is --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Who is he -- I'm sorry to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Major told me that he had no control of the troops who were in the neighbour, on the route towards Nova Kasaba and towards Bratunac.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So looking at your 30th of April 2000 statement, sir, you don't mention that fact anywhere. The only fact that you mention in that statement is that it was "your impression that he was the commander of Major Zoran." Can we please have that put on the e-court for the Lieutenant Colonel, 2D00021 specifically the second paragraph, and last sentence in that paragraph. With the Court's permission, of course. We will just read it in again, Lieutenant Colonel, second paragraph, last sentence, "He introduced himself as Colonel Beara and my impression was that he was the commander of Major Zoran." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is that inaccurate or accurate?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I want to explain that if you let me. When I was at the school, I'd never ever heard of Colonel Beara, his existence. I was there and the interpreter and Major Zoran Malinic, they told me about the Colonel Beara who was the man who could decide about our safety. So the only thing I could see at that time that when he get to us, I gave him the note, typed in Serbo-Croatian, he took the note to Major Zoran, and that's the only thing that I could -- that I've seen as being the commander of. But I don't know -- I didn't verify, I didn't ask him for his passport. I didn't -- that's the only thing that I based it on.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, sir, going back to this tape that was shown to you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: If you'll excuse me, Mr. Ostojic. Can I ask one thing, Mr. Egbers? The fact that Major Zoran Malinic did not have any control over the troops on the route does not necessarily mean that Colonel Beara was a commander to command of Zoran Malinic, would you agree with this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I certainly do agree with you. He told me, this Major Zoran told me that he wasn't in control of the troops and that he had to contact Colonel Beara to get a safe, to get me in safety back to the compound, but I don't know whether Colonel Beara was the commander of the -- of this major. I only know that he visited this Major at the day that I was present there and that I saw him entering the school complaining the things this -- that we discussed yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It might mean on the contrary that Colonel Beara was not the commander of Zoran Malinic.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm sure that we can be informed about that but my impression at that time was that there was a relationship between Colonel Beara and Major Zoran Malinic and that that's it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just a couple more minutes, Your Honour. Isn't it true though that it was Major Zoran who arranged for you to be returned and that was arranged several hours after Mr. Beara left the school or purportedly left the school?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you this again about the tapes that the investigators from the Office of the Prosecution showed you: Isn't it also a fact, sir, that they told me before playing the tape, they said, We believe we have Colonel Beara on this tape, can you watch it and verify it for us?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It didn't happen that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Tell me how it happened.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had to look at it and have to tell them what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, they told you prior to that that they were investigating Mr. Beara, right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sure that it had to be this Colonel Beara because I thought about it before, at the -- but they didn't ask me, this is Colonel Beara, do you recognise him? They showed me the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: How do you know they weren't investigating and wanted you to find in that 54-minute tape Major Zoran Malinic?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That could have been possible as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And they showed you that six- to ten-second tape, correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll read it because six to ten, I don't know whether it's six to ten seconds.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The same sequence or the same amount of tape that we saw yesterday, that's what you looked at basically, correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw the ceremony as I described. It's only the ceremony though shown me.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Lieutenant Colonel, and good luck.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And thank, Your Honours, that's all I have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Ostojic, I think I should have asked you much earlier but can I ask if it is your case that Colonel Beara was not there?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That is correct, Your Honour, and I believe that through evidence that hopefully you'll see that we'll verify that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Who is next? Ms. Condon? Can I have an update on how long do you expect to take, Ms. Condon?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Ten to 20 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President, approximately one half hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Lazarevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. LAZAREVIC
utterances.text: I believe 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Kirgvic or Mr. Josse?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I'm going to go before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's okay. It's not a question of order, it's a question of length of time.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: 20 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 20 minutes. Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 45 minutes, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's always difficult to know but at the moment I'd have said 30 minutes but it will get shorter as time goes by.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right so we can still make it. We can still make it. Yes. Next is Ms. Condon. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Lieutenant Colonel, I want to take you back to your evidence about the relationship between DutchBat and members of the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you mean by the 28th Division.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Well, the 28th Division of the Bosnian Muslim army that was present in the enclave at the time you were there. You agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard about a 28th Division, I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: But you were aware that there were members of the Bosnian Muslim army in the Srebrenica enclave?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I saw was Naser Oric, who was in charge of some men who were -- who were there and who seemed to be armed. I don't know whether that's the 28th Division, you're telling about.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes. Tell me, it was the case, was it not, that the relationship between DutchBat and these men who were armed became quite troubled in spring?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It did.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: It did, didn't it? And your observation posts were robbed by these men that were armed? You had those problems, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were no observation posts robbed by armed men. I don't know what time are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: In spring of 1995.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the spring. I don't have a recollection OP Alpha observation post Alpha being robbed by these men.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: What about the observation posts generally? Did you hear of that? Were there reports of that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the spring time, I can't recollect that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. What about the times when you were reduced to doing your foot -- your patrols on foot because of the lack of fuel?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Obviously that inevitably you're in a very vulnerable position because you're on foot rather than in your APCs, yes?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We are, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You agree with that? Now, you, yourself, you had a perception that at the times that that was going on you why subject to sniper fire from these Muslims who were armed in the enclave. Sorry, you have to actually say "yes" rather than just nod.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I just wait for them to type so I can read it here. It's right that there have been sniper fire by probably the Muslims towards DutchBat, if that's what you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: That's what I'm getting at, yes. And your theory was -- well, before I get to that, naturally, you confronted the people that you perceived were responsible for this, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if DutchBat is, if my patrol is shot at we will return fire or we ask F-16s to support us and the complaining --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I'll just interrupt you. That's before this. This is prior to any issue of close air support. We will get to that. But just this is at the time that I'm talking about in the spring when the relationship starts to deteriorate between DutchBat and the armed Muslims in the enclave, right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is your exact question.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: That you confronted these people who you perceived were sniping at you, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we talked about -- we talked with the Muslims in the enclave of course but there was no -- there wasn't always exactly the location where we were shot at so is it in one of my statements that you're referring to?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: That the issue of you confronting people?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No. This is you were -- you're aware of a book written by David Lloyd [phoen]?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Did you speak to him for that book?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke to him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So tell me about what your theory was in relation to the Muslims sniping at you. Why did you think they were doing that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm sure that we were shot by several Muslims during those days that we were there. They would fire at us from the nearance of the -- let's say the border of the enclave, so that we thought it would be the BSA firing at us and we would return fire to the BSA. That's a theory.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: As to why they were firing at you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: As to why they were firing.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, I just wants to take you to your perception of a soldier, a Muslim soldier. Now, you would agree, would you not, that uniforms weren't always a particularly good indication as to whether or not an able-bodied man in the enclave was an armed -- was a member of the armed unit that was operating in the enclave, whether or not it was the 28th Division or not, you don't know, but you agree with that: Uniforms weren't a good indication?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were very -- there were just a few uniforms worn by Muslims during the fall of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes. But what I'm getting at is that it would not be unusual to see a civilian -- a man who was dressed in civilian clothing armed and in the enclave?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw these men armed during the fall of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And they could be armed but not wearing a uniform, you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You agree with that? Okay. So and incidentally it was your perception, was it not, that in May, that the -- the Muslim -- the Muslims who were armed were in fact flaunting the fact that they had new weapons around that time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes? Now, your evidence in relation to your observations on the 12th of July, and I appreciate I'm jumping around a bit here, but the 12th of July, when you were escorting the first convoy, you saw men on the soccer field, this is the first time you see men on the soccer field and your evidence was here in this Court that they appeared to you to be civilian from the way they were dressed. You accept that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. However, in your debriefing.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Perhaps if the witness could be shown 2D24, Your Honour? At page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, just at the bottom of that document, perhaps if we could scroll down, you say, just, Lieutenant Colonel, do you see where it begins, he saw a great many Serbian fighters on the way?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Do you see that paragraph?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And then you'll see further down, the sentence that begins, "On the way, he saw a football field with hundreds of Muslim prisoners of war in it." You see that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Okay. Now that's the same observation in so far as the first time you're travelling towards Nova Kasaba and you see the men on the soccer field; is that correct? That's the same time?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Only I used --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: It's all right. I just want -- I'm not asking you for an explanation. I'm just -- that's the same time period.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me, Your Honour. I wish she would allow the witness to explain his answer. I think he should always have the right to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're perfectly right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise for entering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Condon, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I used the word prisoner of war and as I did yesterday, considering it wasn't the right term to use. Because I was -- I was then and I'm still a soldier who was thinking in terms of war and prisoners of war. This -- these men were not armed, not armed at that time. I've never heard a shot coming from the direction of the enclave. Those men who were on the football field were civilians to me and I described them as prisoners of war so I'm sure that you're referring to that.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I am and your evidence was exactly in the same terms as you've just given it now yesterday that you said that -- you say, "I used the words POW, I thought those Muslim men had been approached as prisoners of war but of course they were just men who were captured and detained." That's what you said yesterday which is exactly what you said today, so there was no war. So what you say now is that in your mind, the context is different?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you're asking me 11 years later.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes. But that's -- what I'm getting at is that at the time that was the expression you used. Yes? You remember that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And now, retrospectively, your perception is different, you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I filled in all the forms, I was filling in a form describing a war zone. That was in my mind at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: M'hm?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I didn't make a difference between armed fighters who were in uniforms and civilians without uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Now, Your Honour, I may need the assistance of Madam Usher with this document to be placed on the ELMO. This is an attachment to Mr. Egbers's Dutch, original Dutch statement. There's three sketches that were attached to that that had not previously been disclosed to the Defence and I would seek --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You raised this yesterday and I invited you to have a short tete-a-tete with Mr. McCloskey or Ms. Soljan on this. Have you sorted it out?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I intend to use the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm just inquiring whether you have sorted it out. Okay, you may make full use of these sketches any way.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, I apologise, I have marked the document, Your Honour, so the original should really be put up there, if the Prosecution can assist me in that regard. Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment before. What markings did you put on?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Just my highlighting. I prefer the witness not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's okay, it's okay. No words or comments?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Does it exist on e-court? It doesn't?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: That's it, Your Honour. Just for the record, this is -- the document is 00353526.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I'll just gets to you identify this, Mr. Egbers. This is familiar? This has your signature -- perhaps if we could go down to the bottom of the document, Madam Usher, just -- is that your signature?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is my signature but it's not my handwriting so it's not my drawing.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: I just wanted to ask you if it's your signature.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Now, in the course of you -- your Dutch statement having been taken there were in fact a number of three attachments of this nature to your original statement, were there not; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen my statement but I'm sure that this is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes. And this document that we see here is the result of you outlining events that are contained within your statement; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it is an impression of it. The football field isn't drawn right because it's not on that side, I don't know whether you're facing there because that's not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. But there is a football field that is identified here and there is a road that -- it appears on the left-hand side of that that says -- with an arrow, with Mercedes, you see that there?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah? And what -- and then there is bus with refugees, ahead of Mercedes. Is that arrow with the Mercedes, is that you indicating your position?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's me, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Escorting the convoy?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Is that right? So that's certainly correct in so far as the narrative that you were providing to the person who drew this document?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah because you didn't draw it yourself?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. But you were indicating to the person who was drawing the narrative that's reflected; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told her -- I thought it was a her -- that I drove by a football field, that there were Muslims on their knees, that there were civilians.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And uniforms?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And uniforms as well, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So that's correct in so far as it says civilians in uniforms, that is -- that's what you saw, people in uniforms?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes but the people in uniforms were of course not the ones who were on their knees. The men who were on their knees with hands on their neck were Muslims and the uniforms were just standing -- were from the BSA.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: You could read it like they were men in uniforms on their knees with hands on their neck.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: But you shouldn't read it like that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I haven't seen it like that so this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Not accurate. But you signed it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I signed it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You signed it, all right. Now, I want to take you to -- thank you, Madam Usher. Thank you. I want to take you to your evidence in relation to the blocking position that you took up at Bravo 1. Now, I appreciate my learned friend's already asked you some questions about this but I just want to take you to the 9th of July, right? Is that the first time you arrive at the blocking position or not?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there at 8th of July in the evening.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. So that the day of the 9th is your first day at the blocking position; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: My first sunrise there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And the 9th is the day that coincides with the discovery of the M-48 artillery gun; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And that is, I think you said in your evidence, 30 to 40 metres away from your position; is that correct? Is that right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to get a pause.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Sorry. I'll slow down. The next day, being the 10th, Captain Hageman, he's the commander, is he not, of all the -- all four blocking positions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was on the command of Captain Groen and Captain Hageman was in an APC on the market. So I don't know whether he was in command of all the blocking position but I had contact with Captain Groen.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So you had no knowledge of, on the 10th of July, any incident with Captain Hageman's APC being -- going off the road as a result of a hand grenade being thrown at -- by Muslim fighters, you don't know anything about that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about that. I wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. All right. So back to your position on the 10th of July. Is it around the first time you're attacked on the 10th of July at Bravo 1, just so that I understand how many times you come under fire on the 10th of July, is it around what time of day, the first time you're attacked?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was in the morning but if you want to know exactly I've got to --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: That's all right. You can't tell me. That's all right. And you had up there with you two forward air controllers; is that right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, there were English SAS colleagues at my -- with me, and I don't know whether they had the opportunity to forward air control from that site but we had to have Dutch forward air controllers at my position.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So you had two Dutch forward air controllers?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time, I asked for one Dutch forward air controller to come to my position.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: So he was there?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether it was in the morning that he was there but he came from.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: At some stage?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: From Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. Now the significance of having the forward air controllers, there is obviously for the link in terms of calling in closed air support, isn't that --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Or air strikes, but they are the ones, they have to contact the planes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, after the attack, this first attack, you contacted or via another person, you contacted Captain Groen, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sure I contacted him every ten minutes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: M'hm. And he wanted to know from you, did he not, well, where was the source of the fire coming from?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Obvious question, yes?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. And you weren't sure, were you? You weren't 100 per cent sure?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was sure it was Bosnian Serb fire coming from a tank but I wasn't sure whether they were firing at me at the time or at the piece of artillery that was 40 metres nearby. That's why I asked the Bosnian Muslims not to fire the gun and I couldn't be 100 per cent sure that they were firing at me because I wasn't hit at that time. There were shrapnels going through the APC and I had a light injury but I wasn't 100 per cent sure at that time, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: That you were the target; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, you've indicated that you'd asked the Muslim -- was there a commander there in the artillery -- how many soldiers did you see around the artillery piece?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eight to ten soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Sorry?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Eight to ten.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And they were all armed, I presume?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not all.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Not all? So you spoke to the commander or someone who appeared to be in charge around the artillery piece and you said well, don't fire it while we are in the area, yes?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: He gave you an undertaking that that would happen, did he?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wrote a note, and the road was taken by a courier to his commander. But it was never fired.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. As far as you're aware, as far as you're aware?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yeah. But tell me, because I obviously wouldn't know, is an M-48, is that something that can destroy a tank? Is it capable of that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You wouldn't know?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would be guessing like you. That wouldn't be proper.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Would you like me to guess?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: No, please don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: You could -- the witness can be shown 2D23, please, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: This is one of your debriefing statements, Mr. Egbers, if I could just take to you paragraph 3 of that document, you see that there? The heading, did the BiH do anything to stop the BSA attack. Do you see that there?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: It says, "Yes, observation of artillery in the area of my observation post, B1," so that's Bravo 1?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: "BiH patrol in the direction of BSA tank eliminated." What did that mean?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, can I explain to you what I meant?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: M'hm.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because there was a group of Muslims who went through Bravo 1 and said we'll try to go to the south and try to eliminate the tank. That's what they intended to do but it wasn't by firing this piece of artillery.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Even though it says there it seems to be a foregone conclusion there that a tank was eliminated but that's wrong?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: If that's wrong, that's fine.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't be sure that they really succeeded. They told me that they did. That's what they told me but I had no vision of it so you'd better ask the BSA whether it's true or not.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, I want to take you to later on in the day of the 10th of July. Just so I understand the sequence of events is it that again on the afternoon of the 10th of July, you were fired upon when you were heading back to -- is that correct, back to base?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I was on the 10th of July I was fired upon by the BSA by a tank and when I drove towards the market place, there was some AK 47 fire from a Muslim fighter.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: All right. And when you got back to base, you indicated in one of your debriefing statements that the Muslims had looted the UNHCR warehouse. I can show you where you said that but you accept that that's true?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Now, with -- when you say the UNHCR warehouse, can you be a little bit more specific at all about what building that was in the town of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was a building on the market place in Srebrenica, and when I saw that night that there was -- there were people coming in and they were carrying goods out that's strange of course in a war zone.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Well, strange as well also because no doubt you would have observed in your six months period there that while there were goods supposedly -- there were goods coming in through the UNHCR there was a problem with distribution of those goods amongst the civil population, wasn't there?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no -- I have no information about that. That was another section. I was just in the north of the enclave.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Right. But you had your own views about whether or not there was a black market going on within the enclave run by Naser Oric, didn't you? You thought he was the head of it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've never declared anything about Naser Oric being the head of the black market.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: That's not right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have any recollection of ever declaring about Naser Oric being head of the black market. I know that there was a kind of black market but you should ask these questions to others.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Just in relation to the goods that you saw coming out of the UNHCR warehouse, can you be a little bit more specific, what, about sacks of rice, flour? What did you see?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was norm -- it was flour.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Anything else?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw flour brought out.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: And that was by the civilian population doing that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. I thank you, Ms. Condon. Who is next? Mr. Bourgon? Go ahead. We will have a break at 10.30, Mr. Bourgon.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Good morning, Colonel.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I have a few questions for you, well, first let me confirm I mentioned that to you when we met yesterday or the day before, that I represent Drago Nikolic in this case, and I have a few questions for you in respect of the situation as you lived it in July of 1995. First I'd like to confirm with you that you did not -- during your stay in Srebrenica, you did not see or have access to any orders or any other internal documents, whether from the ABiH or from the BSA. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen any orders from both sides.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So would you agree with me that other than what you could see, you could not tell what they wanted to accomplish at any one time?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be more specific? I don't know where you're aiming at.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Well, simply, if you see, you assume that they are doing something but you don't have anything on paper saying that this is what they are trying to do, according to the orders that were issued?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I haven't seen any written orders by BSA. I only saw the troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So you don't know what they were trying to accomplish throughout your time in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Other than what from what you can see?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Of course, I've seen what they are doing. When you're on the road and you see eight or ten Muslims with hands in their neck with two infantry BSA soldiers with them I don't have to have a written report that they were transporting them to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Absolutely agree with you. That's not what I'm referring to. I'm referring to in terms of the army of the Serbian army, the Bosnian Serb army, in terms of their goal in launching the attack on Srebrenica enclave.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: You did not know that others than from what you can see and then guess based on your experience?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He answered that already.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will answer that because I was in a school room with this Major Zoran Malinic and he had all maps of the enclave and he had some observation posts on it and he had some marks on it as well in the south of the enclave. So that's what I saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, in your -- as part of your testimony, you mentioned in response to a question from one of my colleagues that you saw an artillery piece, as a matter of fact an M-48, which belonged to the Muslims in the enclave, and that was close to your position?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And this would have taken place according to your testimony in Krstic, the second day that you took your blocking position?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you did see during your stay in the -- during that time frame that you adopted or took your blocking position, you did see a number of armed Muslim men in the village?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen them, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, yesterday you mentioned a relatively low number of 60 [Realtime transcript read in error "630"], because others have said 1500, but can we agree that there were lots of armed men that you saw in that village mixed with the population?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw a lot of armed men but not 1500, oh, no, not more than 100. I said 60. That was what I thought was correct at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, these soldiers that you saw, they were armed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The transcript page 32, line 20 should read 60 instead of 630.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I just want to ask you of you that the armed men that you saw?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Bourgon, take a note of your transcript, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I will slow down. Didn't happen last time I thought I was okay, but -- let's not get excited.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Colonel, the men you saw in town who were armed and the men you saw around your blocking position and the men you saw who were handling the artillery piece, these people were defending against the BSA attack; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, looking at your own position in this situation, as a member of DutchBat, you had rules of engagement which were limited to self defence; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And self defence, according to the UN, that means that unless you are fired upon, that means a member of DutchBat, you're not to use deadly force?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, at the time you went to the blocking position, you recall receiving a green order saying, Forget the rules of engagement, now we defend?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I had no such order given to me that we had to defend that line, especially we didn't fire at the BSA from my APC. We could only reach for 800 metres with our gun on top of the APC. We did not fight the BSA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But in yourself, you did get fire upon your position, both by the Muslims and by the BSA?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And you confirm that on 11 of July, there was close air support and there were some Dutch fighters who did take hostile action against the Bosnian Serb army?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, at that point, will you agree with me that as far as the Bosnian Serb army is concerned, DutchBat is no longer a friendly force?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's a strange conclusion. We did not -- we did not fire at the BSA from my position. We were on top of a hill with a white vehicle, with blue helmets. We were not acting green like hitting in a wood and firing at the enemy. We were still a line inside of the enclave, not to cross. There was no -- we were no army fighting the BSA.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I appreciate this, Colonel but the Dutch fighters who fired upon those tanks, would agree with me that they can be associated with DutchBat?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only with DutchBat, I think they were two Dutch F-16s but they could have as well been English but anything else.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Let's say the UN to be more precise?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: To be more precise, the UN, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I'd like to address the way between Srebrenica and Potocari, when the population started to move along with yourself and a couple of DutchBat vehicles. If I suggest to you that this movement towards Potocari was actually initiated by the UN, because the population was panicking and did not know what to do, would that be --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That it would be correct. We tried to get them out of Srebrenica towards Potocari.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, at that time, you mentioned in response to my colleague that you don't know what the 28 Division is and I was caught by surprise because I had a question prepared for this, but you were aware that all the armed men from the enclave had left or left on the 11th of July, were you aware of this?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't aware of that during my time at the enclave at the blocking position.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And the existence of the 28th Division as an armed component, you're not aware of that either when you're there?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when we talk about a division, in our army terms, it's a lot of men, armed, weapons, and I think that a division isn't the right word for these men who had AK 47s.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, when you testified in the Krstic case, you went at length on this topic, saying, how weak and unorganised Muslim army was and that it could not hold the pressure of the Bosnian Serb army. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing that they did was small groups who tried to eliminate the tank. They had some fighters with AK 47s and some RPGs to fire at the tank. That was the only resistance there was and there was us standing between those Muslim fighters at the time and the BSA. There were no tanks or just one piece of artillery what didn't fire when I was there.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So Srebrenica was, in fact, poorly defended?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the weapons in the weapon collection point were given up by the Muslims when it was a safe area as you know. There was no line of defence. There were observation posts from the UN around the enclave. There was no side by side defence of the enclave, as you suggest.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Let me make my question more precise. In the events in which you lived in those days between 8 of July going up to 11th of July, there was a defence put forward trying to defend the city of Srebrenica but it was not a very good defence?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was -- there were only a few men with guns trying to eliminate tanks. That was the only thing they could do. There were no Muslims with tanks or other equipment, just like the BSA had.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now my question is not whether there are tanks or Muslim tanks. My question is simply that they were defending the city of Srebrenica to the best of their ability in the circumstances?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were the only one who reacted at the attack of the enclave but I don't know whether you can call it a defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, given that the Muslim army was as you say maybe not well organised, that's probably the reason why they decided to leave or could -- would be a good reason for them to decide to leave.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this is a very strange question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: One moment, Colonel. If you think that in answering that question you would need to speculate, please ask not to answer that question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't want any speculation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No. I'm sure that you don't want it either. So I wasn't aware of the men leaving the enclave that I was in the Bravo 1 position and I don't know whether -- whether -- why they did it. You could ask them.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, I'm just going to ask you, did you at any point see by the men who were trying to put up a defence of Srebrenica, did you at any time see a sign of surrender?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no recollection of anyone surrendering to the BSA, by a Muslim male at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, again we look at the once you're on your way between Srebrenica and Potocari, you mentioned in your testimony in the Krstic case, and that is on page 2219, lines 15 to 17, you mentioned that there was shelling around you on both sides of the road. Do you recall saying that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now you would agree with me that there wasn't any shelling on the convoy itself or on the column of refugees with your vehicles going back to Potocari?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time that I was there, there were grenades falling, 20, 30, 40 metres from the colony but I don't know what happened after I left there of course. But the only thing I can describe to you is that there were no people killed at the time, that there were no people killed at that time by that shelling.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Just one quick -- because in the Krstic case you said 100 metres. Would that be more accurate?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: From -- because when a grenade hits the floor at ten metres you'll be killed so it must be further away but --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, you -- you mentioned at that time that you picked up on your own vehicle, on your own APC that you picked up some people who were ill, you say, "I picked up the ill people," and that is page 2220, lines 18 to 20. So you recall picking up people on your APC?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the Medecins Sans Frontieres, they had a hospital in -- inside that and they asked me whether it was safe for them to say and we said, "Oh, no, you've got to leave as well." So they brought on to my APC some sick people who were in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, the purpose of my question is just to clarify with you that the people who were on your APC, they came from the hospital, they are not people that you pick up along the way because they get injured?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: They came from the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And how many vehicles, how many APCs from DutchBat were there carrying these people?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only tell you about my own vehicle, that was where they were brought on to, I don't know whether other vehicles transported ill people as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: And how many people can you fit in your APC, injured people from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, they were not only in my APC but above it as well because we drove very slowly. It could have been 20, 20 people.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That would be the maximum, would you agree with me, 20 on an APC?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I -- when I crossed the UN base of the Bravo Company, I saw everything that could drive was full of people that wanted protection from the UN so there were hundreds of people on one APC so it could have been more but on my APC, it was just 20.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, just to clarify, there is a difference between people trying to get away and climbing to an APC, and people injured that you put on your own APC?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: So when I speak about 20, 20 people that came from the hospital is quite a large amount for one APC?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Okay. Now, the next day, after of course sleeping 12 hours, which was no doubt well deserved, you were involved in the escorting of convoys. My first question in relation to this is that you actually escorted two convoys between Potocari and Kladanj, both of these convoys had a number of buses and I just want to confirm that these convoys made it to Kladanj and that you did not see any ill treatment of anybody on those convoys during that time?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think we discussed that already. There were two convoys, the first convoy was properly with 50 people in a bus and later on it get -- there were more people in buses and what I saw happened to the women and children was that they were leaving the buses at Kladanj and walked the way towards the Muslim area.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: But my question is quite precise: You didn't see anybody on one of those buses being ill treated?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when you load up the bus and you push them inside the bus, that's ill treatment, of course, but I haven't seen them beating them. That's not what I can recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Now, in between the two convoys that you escorted to Kladanj, you went into the "White House" and I just wants could confirm that when you went into this "White House" you saw people who were scared but you did not see any ill treatment taking place in the "White House"?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That's what you said in the Krstic case when you testified. But you also added something. You added that when you were asked about -- when you asked inside the "White House" about these persons, you were shown a pile of knives that were taken from these persons and you were told that they wanted to, of course, disarm them to ensure that no bus drivers would be attacked or hurt. You recall saying that in the Krstic case? I can quote your words if you want?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll just answer after. You're going too fast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think you should actually quote chapter, verse, page and verse.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: Mr. President, this is on page 2231 from the testimony of the witness in the Krstic case. Sorry, 2230, lines 2 to 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Can you read it out, please, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I got the wrong reference, I'm sorry. I will find the reference after a few minutes and come back to this so we don't waste any time.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I can recall that there was a story of course by the BSA why they should separate the men from the women.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But that's -- it's related to the --

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: I now have the reference, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's why I wanted it read out. Yes, Mr. Bourgon?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: The question was, "Did you have a conversation with any of the Bosnian Serb soldiers who were there?" And the witness answered: "I did. I asked them why would you separate the men from the women? And he pointed out that a lot of knives, just pocket knives, that were lying there and said, 'Well, you see, they are all armed with knives and we don't want them to attack one of our bus drivers.'" . Do you recall this?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOURGON
utterances.text: That's all I wanted to -- now, as you exited from the "White House," actually, money was offered to you by some of the men to say, "Take us away," because they were scared. You recall that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Money was offered to me because it was useless to them so it wasn't money offered to me so -- "Can you arrange something for me," but it was given to me so because they were sure that it wasn't of any value to them.
