utterances.text: And was there any rumour as to how these people had died?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: None at all?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not -- the rumour didn't reach me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And I simply want to deal with your state of knowledge at the time, that's why I'm going to ask this question. Were you making at that time any assumption as to how they had died?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Fine. I'll move on. As I say I want to return if I may briefly to this issue of the wounded. You have told us that you didn't go to the hospital. MSF brought to you the wounded and you were able to effectively escort them to Potocari; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would replace the word escort into bringing them to Potocari. They were on my APC.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And the occupants of the hospital included the sick and ill as opposed to people who had been wounded?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, in my statements, it says the ill and wounded but I can't recall that there were wounded people. Their bodies were complete, as I recall it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I think that's fair, if I may say, because perhaps the easiest way to deal with this at page 2261 of your evidence in the Krstic trial, you confirmed in the course of cross-examination that, "There were only sick people as well as mentally ill people as well as women who were carrying babies on my vehicle, and I don't know whether there were wounded from shelling which happened from the 6th of July," which I think clarifies what you've just said.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Thank you for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: So these wounded people --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We just called them ill people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Thank you very much. Arrive in Potocari and we know that, and I am now going to use the word wounded because that's the word that has been used elsewhere in this trial, wounded people left Potocari on the 17th of July. Were you involved in any of the negotiations that led up to those people leaving?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Did you have anything to do between the 11th of July and the 17th of July with people who were either ill or wounded and were in Potocari?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I did was to bring the people from the APC towards the hospital inside the compound at the headquarters UN. That's the only thing I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: And do you have any knowledge of these ill or wounded people being handed over to the ICRC?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only know that they have left the headquarters of DutchBat at any time after all the refugees have left but I don't know whether they were handed over to another organisation.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: So you're confirming you literally had no involvement in those events at all?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Finally I should have asked you this, going back if I may to the 10th and 11th of July, and the evacuation of the Srebrenica hospital, did any information get to you from the MSF or any other source that people had been killed in the hospital as a result of shelling?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't informed about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: You were not informed about that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOSSE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you, Mr. Josse. And finally we have got Mr. Haynes, who is appearing for Mr. Pandurevic. Try to leave us about five minutes, Mr. Haynes. Not five hours. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Mr. Egbers, can we agree please that the day of the NATO air strikes was the 11th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We can.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that was the day after two members of your crew had been injured with shrapnel?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And that was the second day that you went to position B 1 in the south of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: So you'll agree with me, won't you, then, that the first day you went to position B 1 in the south of the enclave was the 9th of July and you were there for three days, not the 8th of July, as you said in chief?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the night that Raviv van Renssen died, that was the 8th of July. I got the order to go to the south and then at the end of the day during the night I had to go to Bravo 1 and I counted that few hours of day July 8 as day number 1, and we stayed overnight there so --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He explained that before.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, the position that you took up, B 1, was on the red road that went south from Srebrenica to Zelani Jadar, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether the road was red.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It was an asphalt road.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it wasn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It was a made road rather than a dirt track or anything like that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: But I thought it was yellow on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm going to have a map put on the ELMO in front of you --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: -- in the hope that you can help us as to where position B 1 was?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will. So it's not on the red but in the yellow and it's on the second angle. Can you see that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. For the record, one moment, for the record, the witness indicates a spot to the south of the winding road on the map which is immediately at 10 minutes from the number 448, which appears above Bajramovici, between Stupina on the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Your Honour, I really don't mind if he marks the map. I can bear the expense.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Then you can mark the map.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. And could you put there then the -- what that indicates? B 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And sign your signature or your initials, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. And you will tender this later, Mr. Haynes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was that a position that was predetermined you should go to or was it a position you chose yourself to take?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was a position Captain Groen and I agreed as a position to have a clear view in the south of the enclave. So I knew the position because it was the way to OP Alpha and I drove it a lot and he also indicated that that was the best spot for the blocking position.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And when you took up that position you found yourself 40 metres away from a Muslim artillery battery, that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 9th of July, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did that surprise you or were you expecting to find that battery there?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: It surprised me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And whilst you were there, you came under fire?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm not unnecessarily through constraint of time going to call up documents to show you but what you said in your witness statement was there were five shells fired at you in succession. Do you stand by that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: At least.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were at least five shells.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I may have to show you your witness statement what you said is five shells were fired at you in succession. Was that right or wrong what you said on the 24th of October 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was shelled several times, so do you indicate the first shelling or the second shelling?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Soljan?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: I believe it would be a good idea to show the witness what he was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's 2D19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's proceed with showing the witness the relative document, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's page 3.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Read it from the top. It's the sentence that begins at the end of the third line. Now that you've refreshed your memory do you recall that five shots were fired in succession?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this refers to the first shelling. It says they fired five times in succession, but after that, we had another order to come back and we got shelled again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, I'm really only concerned with --

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: These five.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: -- the position you took on the 9th of July. Were you fired upon five times?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do agree with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. And the result of that was that two of your men and the commander of the Muslim artillery battery were injured, weren't they?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't call it an artillery battalion -- how do you call it?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The commander, the Muslim artillery unit, whatever. I'm not going to pick a fight with you over the term. We know what we are talking about.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Two of your men and the commander of the Muslim artillery unit were injured?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were they injured by the fifth of the five shots or one in the middle?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't recall that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And after that, you removed yourself from that position to a position several hundred metres lower down the hill, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. I can point it out to you where it was if you would like to.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm not too worried about that at the moment?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: In evidence-in-chief to Ms. Soljan, and for those who want a reference, it was on October the 18th, page 89, lines 10 to 17, you said you were in that position on the 9th of July for ten minutes. Would that be right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was there several times that day, and during the first ten minutes we got shelled. But it was on the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, please forgive me, are you saying that you went down the hill and back up again and down the hill and back up again or that you were only there once and got shelled and you went back to a safe position?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were other APCs in the south and they had no radio contact with the commander, OP Bravo, at the Bravo Company, so via my APC, there could be radio contact but only when I was nearby Bravo 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that was another order so to go back to Bravo 1, although we were shelled, to stay there in position.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You'll agree with me, won't you, that that is something that's plainly absent from your witness statement, if you read your witness statement it appears that you were there, shot at five times, and then you retreated to position several hundred metres below.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I told you, that's what we did the first time we got shelled. But then afterwards, we got another order to go back into Bravo 1, the original position.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Would you go down that page? According to that witness statement the only order you received that day was to return to Srebrenica, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: What are you referring to? Because when I saw later on, later that afternoon I saw about 50 Bosnian Serb soldiers had reached the summits of Srebrenica then I was back at the original Bravo 1 site again. So we got shelled we had to go to another position, had the order to come back to original Bravo 1 and again and then after another shelling we even had our way to the other position shelled.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I see. So the witness statement should in fact read that you were shelled five times, then you went back and got shelled some more?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: We were shelled a lot.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I see. Now, during the course of your being in position B 1, you saw a Bosnian Serb tank, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And will you agree with me I don't want you -- again to take you through various references you only ever saw one tank?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: On that day, the 9th of July.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I only saw a T 54/55 entering and then leaving. I don't know whether it was the same tank who was coming back again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You said when you gave evidence before in this Tribunal in the Krstic case that that tank was about three kilometres away?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder whether you would be so good as to mark the position of the tank on the map.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks] You saw a tank coming into the enclave. I don't know the exact route he took but from this position I could see all the way up here to Pusmulici and to this side of the enclave. He came from east into the enclave but I don't know the exact road.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Would you kindly write "tank" inside that rectangle, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And an arrow pointing to --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yeah, all right.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I want to be clear what your evidence today, your evidence is you could see a tank from that position where you were?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you notice its barrel position?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you be more specific?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. Was its barrel horizontal or pointing upwards?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Pointing upwards because we have learned that it could only fire 1500 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I wonder when you first learned that and from whom.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what we learn in the royal military academy when we all learn about equipment, and it's even in a small UN book, I guess.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Captain Groen was very concerned to know whether you had been targeted by Serb fire, wasn't he?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Because on the 9th of July, you weren't under a green order, you were still under blue orders, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've always been under blue orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And so your rules of engagement dictated that you were not allowed to fire upon the Serb forces unless they targeted you directly?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But when Captain Groen asked you whether you'd been targeted by the Serb forces on the 9th of July, your answer was you couldn't confirm that?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, because there was a piece of artillery nearby.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I want to move, please, to the next day, and I'm going to deal with it as briefly as I can. The following day, you were required to go back to B 1 at 7.00 in the morning; that's right, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's possible. I don't know the date and the times.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, there was a very specific purpose to your going to B 1 on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: There was air strike expected at 700 hours precisely?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And you went there with forward air controllers to call in that air strike?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Again, when you reached B 1, you were under fire again, you say?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether that was on 7.00 in the morning but at that time we didn't had to stand on B 1 as a site because we had to install the forward air controllers.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And again you were only there for about ten minutes?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I wasn't. I was there for hours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, again, 2D19, please. And I'm going to take you to the lower half of the page the next day, the 10th of July, and the last but one paragraph.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I told you, when you look at the other paragraph, the next day, Monday, the 10th of July I returned with my group to a safe place in the vicinity of the original location. That's where I stand hours. And I can show it to you on the map. It's nearby and that's why we didn't go all in the open because we had to have a -- forward air controllers make contact to air planes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I stood here. Shall I show it to you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks]. I said forward air controller over there. And that's where we stayed. Then we got the order to go back to the original position, and that's where we got shelled again.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Where is the safe place that you refer to?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what I just pointed out here at the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Could you mark it "safe place," please?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Marks].

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Was the forward air controller in your APC?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He wasn't at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And to what was he intended to call air strikes?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: He -- they told me and my commander at that time, that there would be an air strike with a gun ship on every target in the south of the enclave that's not UN. That's why we had to go back there at 7.00. So the only thing he had to do was to point out where the UN vehicles were.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: He didn't have to direct the aircraft to the targets?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know his exact mission. I think that within close air support there is a contact between the forward air controller and the planes but I don't know whether it's also in case of an air strike.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Now, I want to be clear what you're saying about what you saw of the air strikes themselves. Because you'll see on the document before you that you said in your witness statement of the 24th of October of 1995 that two Dutch -- that the Dutch F-16s then knocked two Bosnian Serb tanks out of action.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, that's no air strike but close air support I think and there were two Dutch F-16s and they were pointed at a tank who was in -- near Bravo 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Well, what is it a tank or two tanks?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you see the result of the air strikes?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you hear them?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've heard an explosion and we could hear the tank moving into -- coming into our position because it has an engine that can be heard of course, and I couldn't hear that any more so they switched it off or -- but it wasn't in use.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You see, you've said a number of things about the air strikes in the course of your witness statements and testimonies. In the Krstic trial you said that there were two tanks which disappeared after the air strikes. Is that right or wrong?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall that but the only thing I can tell you is that they were not functioning at that time any more. I'm sure that they didn't disappear.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: What you said to Mr. Ostojic when he was asking you questions yesterday was that there was one strike which was -- one tank which stopped firing at you.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I didn't hear the engine running and it didn't fire at us any more. So that's the only -- I can't draw a conclusion whether the tank was hit, whether it was demolished or not. It didn't fire at us and we could go to Srebrenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Could you see it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I couldn't hear it any more. I couldn't see a tank burning.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a short video clip, please, and see whether this is reminiscent of anything you saw. And this is from the Srebrenica trial video. 01577 at four minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you see vehicles like that having been destroyed on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you see vehicles like that in the vicinity of B 1 when you were there on the 10th of July?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen them.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you see ambulances or other vehicles?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I saw ambulances but it was in the Pusmulici area.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Moving on very, very rapidly, your platoon operated ordinarily in the northwest sector of the enclave that's correct, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Did you as it were, work exclusively there during the period January to July of 1995?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You moved about in other parts of the enclave?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Had you ever been to the south and to Pusmulici?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've been there in July, before the observation post fell but I don't know whether I actually was at the village of Pusmulici. I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It is a village, though, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are houses, so it must be a village.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: It's some little distance from the main town of Srebrenica itself?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a difference between those small groups of houses and the -- was that your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: You wouldn't call it, would you, a suburb of the north of Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It was small, smaller than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Were you only able to see Pusmulici when you were in the elevated position at B 1 or could you see it still when you were down the hill in your safe position?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could see them from both positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: And what could you see of it?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when I looked at it and I reported that there was smoke coming out of the houses and there were men there and I've seen dogs but that's -- that could only be seen by binocular.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I mean, just coming to the end now, looking down at the map may help you, by looking at the contours, remind yourself of the sort of terrain in the area of the south of Srebrenica. You can see they place contour lines together in the way the road follows the contours of the hills.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And what's your question, sir?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I'm suggesting it's not very easy to see any great distance in that area, binoculars or no binoculars.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, what I saw was smoke coming out of that direction. We've had a map and we assumed that it would be Pusmulici.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I haven't been there.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: I just want to check that that's what your evidence is. You saw smoke coming out of the houses, you had a map, and you assumed it would be Pusmulici.

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because I knew where I was and I knew the distance.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: But that's the extent of what you could see, smoke coming out of the house?

utterances.speaker: VINCENTIUS BERNARDUS EGBERS [Resumed]
utterances.text: And people entering the houses and infantry along the houses but I didn't see the fire coming out of the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: Yes. Well, it's 1.40. I'm going to stop there, I think.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you so much, Mr. Haynes. Is there re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any questions from the Bench? None? So there are two matters that we would like to address, but both need to be addressed in private session. So let's go into -- yes. In the meantime, before we do so, Colonel, we have finished with you. I thank you so much on behalf of the Trial Chamber for having come to give evidence, and we wish you a safe journey back to wherever you're going.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. So let's go into -- we can finalise the documents first.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Defence teams, have you been given a list of the documents that the Prosecution is seeking to tender through the -- this witness? Do you have any objection to any of them? Mr. Ostojic?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour, I would object to P02025.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. And that's for the reasons that you explained when the matter was first raised, or this one, the video and what's the reason for your objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In addition to the reasons that I cited to the court before but also because we were never given any foundation of the video and we were also -- from the witness's testimony as I recall it, is that the witness was given this video in a suggestive manner which is improper and should be prohibited to make an identification of an accused or an individual. So for all those reasons that I mentioned initially and then these two that it's an improper foundation, not authenticated, there is no date of when this video was taken and I think the Court wasn't given opportunity to look at the entirety of the video, which is splices from many different videos, I think that it would be something that should not be introduced in evidence and the Court should reject it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any other objections to any other of the documents sought to be tendered? None?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So the decision of the Trial Chamber in relation to this P2025 is a unanimous one and it is for rejecting your objection, Mr. Ostojic, on the basis that your allegations do not appear to be founded or substantiated by any evidence and, in addition, we have taken into consideration the relevance of this document. The documents that are being tendered and admitted are P01664, P401661 -- 1688, PIC 19, P02025, P01901, PIC 20, PIC 21, with the following 65 ter numbers, 2111. And then there are Defence documents that are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mr. Beara -- Mr. Ostojic, do you have any documents that you wish to tender?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, 2D00019, 20, 24 and 25.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So what about 20, 21, 22 and 23?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We will not be tendering those at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Are there any objections from the Prosecution in relation to 19, 24 and 25?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: No objections, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, any other Defence team would like to tender any documents? Ms. Condon?

utterances.speaker: MS. CONDON
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. Your Honour I'd seek to tender the document that was shown to Mr. Egbers that was the diagram attached to his Dutch statement, that's ERN number 00353526.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you. Any objections? No? So it is tendered and will be given an identification number, Exhibit number. Any other of the Defence teams? Mr. Haynes?

utterances.speaker: MR. HAYNES
utterances.text: The map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The map, yes. Same applies to the map that has been marked by the witness. Yes, Madam Fauveau?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, 5D67 an UNMO report dated 12th of July 1995, and 5D77, 5D78, 5D79 and 5D81, excerpts from the NIOD report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. So they are admitted. Any further? None? So we can close that chapter. You will all recall -- let's go into private session, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SOLJAN
utterances.text: My apologise, Your Honour. There was an additional OTP witness statement dated April 30th, 2000, which was discussed in great detail by the Defence for Mr. Beara on I believe yesterday, on the 19th. It is marked 2D00021 and we would like that to be admitted, in fact, since it was discussed to a great extent and identified to Mr. Beara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Any objection?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, if they wish to use that exhibit they should have been forthright, and they weren't. And quite candidly I do object to it. We asked the questions on that exhibit specifically relating to that. We think it's a short exhibit. It's all on the record. I think it will muddy it if the Court even looks at that exhibit. The witness even references a 96 statement that apparently he gave that we still haven't obtained, so I think it would just really confuse the record and wouldn't benefit us. We have his testimony on the specific issues within that exhibit. That's why I didn't think it was appropriate to offer it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is it an exhibit? Is it an exhibit? Exactly. This is what I -- what if it is never tendered by --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: It's not tendered by our team. What I think the Court's ruling --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How can the evidence then become intelligible if you never tender it?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think the Court ruled on it with other exhibits. You said we covered it clearly in our examination and it's not necessary to have it as duplicate evidence but I'll obviously have to defer to what the Court says, if you think it's necessary, but I'd like the 96 statement. Plus it was never asked anything in redirect by the Prosecutor on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The position is as follows: Once it has been made use of, the Prosecution has every right to seek the admission of this document. So this is being admitted and then you need to take care of how you number it. Nothing further? I understand Mr. McCloskey that you wanted to address the Trial Chamber. I implore the staff to bear with us a couple of more minutes. We'll soon be finished. Mr. McCloskey?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, just very briefly on just a scheduling matter, and especially while I have everyone here, Mr. Bourgon has asked to ask us to see if we could change some of our scheduling for November because he has a very important, I think, opportunity that may take him away from the place and the witnesses are very important and we are endeavouring to do that and move some witnesses from November into December. I think we can do that and we are making every effort to do that. He much course needs -- would like to have a commitment and I will give him that commitment as much as I can, and I think we will be able to make it with witnesses, and we are endeavouring to, that everyone will see that that will change what we filed a bit. As long as everyone is on board for that, then we will continue to do it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I suggest that you finalise this exercise and that you communicate it to everyone. And then we'll see but of course, I think your suggestion --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's all I needed to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let's go into private session for a couple of minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Registrar, could you kindly convey to the registrar, your boss, the Trial Chamber's appreciation and gratitude for the patience and cooperation shown by all the staff, technicians, translators, and everyone else. We will reconvene on Wednesday, starting with the testimony of the next witness who I suppose will be the witness that will come in the afternoon. In other words you're not bringing Koster before him?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No. It will be Mr. Groenewegen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 25th day of October, 2006, at 2.15 p.m. 20 21 22 23 24 25
